title: V2 VERIFY (rotation slot 2): full adversarial replay of the bridge enforcement and reputation.py
description: CONTROL-PLANE TIER per P-024: full adversarial replay, not a brief one. Both artifacts are control-plane code. Four attacks are mandatory and each is a REJECT if it succeeds where it should fail or fails where it should succeed: attempt an overrule WITHOUT the embedded predecessor and confirm refusal; attempt to make reputation.py write ANYTHING and confirm it cannot; verify the sybil caveat appears on EVERY output path including --json; and verify Phase A neutrality, that no code path varies any burden by standing. Then check the shipped code against T-368's numbered requirements one by one - a green suite hides an unimplemented requirement that no test covers. Verdict T-370 and T-371 separately.
acceptance_criteria: RE-RUN BOTH SUITES YOURSELF; do not trust the handoffs. `python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" -v` with N > 229 and `python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_reputation*.py" -v` with N >= 12, both with your own 'Ran N tests' lines quoted, plus `python3 -m py_compile .harness/bin/precedent.py` and `python3 -m py_compile .harness/bin/reputation.py`, both exit 0. Exit 0 alone is not evidence (P-025).

ATTACK 1 - THE OVERRULE WITHOUT ITS PREDECESSOR, in a temp root: paste the exact command, the exact stderr message and exit code 1. Then attempt it WITH the ratio but each authorship element missing in turn (record id, published_by, issuing task) and confirm refusal each time with a message naming the missing element. Then run the compliant version and confirm exit 0 AND that the stored field holds the predecessor's ratio byte-for-byte together with all three authorship elements. THEN TRY TO BYPASS THE REFUSAL: at least three bypass shapes (an empty-string embedding, whitespace-only, a truncated or paraphrased ratio, a wrong-record ratio, --voids or --supersedes instead of --overrules) - list each attempt and its result. A refusal any flag combination defeats is a REJECT.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: an ordinary publish with no --overrules is completely unaffected. If the enforcement taxes ordinary publishes, REJECT - the enforcement is a condition on one verb, not a new tax on the registry.

ATTACK 2 - MAKE reputation.py WRITE SOMETHING AND CONFIRM IT CANNOT: hash every store (each .harness/precedents/*.json, .harness/blackboard.json, .harness/state.json) and count .harness/logs/events.jsonl lines before and after invoking EVERY subcommand and EVERY output path - including --json and every error path (unknown flag, missing identity, nonexistent identity, empty registry, unreadable root). Paste the hashes and counts. ONE BYTE OF DRIFT IS A REJECT. Also grep the source for log_event, open(...,'w'), atomic_write_json, append_jsonl and lock acquisition, and report every hit with its context.

ATTACK 3 - THE SYBIL CAVEAT ON EVERY OUTPUT PATH (AB3): enumerate every output path in the code yourself, then run each and grep the caveat line CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER against the spec's quoted text, including --json where it must be a named field rather than prose. A single path without it is a REJECT, because a consequence-wiring consumer reads whichever path it happens to call.

ATTACK 4 - PHASE A NEUTRALITY (AB4): read the code, do not take the docstring's word. Confirm NO code path varies any verification or confirmation burden by standing, in reputation.py AND in precedent.py - diff precedent.py against git HEAD and confirm qualifying_applications_count, the confirm verb's identity floor, and REITERATION_N are untouched by this epic. Confirm reputation.py exports nothing importable as a gate. A standing-keyed threshold anywhere is a REJECT.

PER-FIGURE ATTRIBUTION AND EMPTY-NOT-FABRICATED (AB2): every figure names its source store; the adjudications figure is present, empty, and explicitly marked unavailable. Then RECOMPUTE at least one figure yourself from the raw records and confirm the number matches - an attributed wrong number is worse than an unattributed one, because attribution is what makes it believable.

AB9-1 VISIBILITY: every consolidation figure shows WHO confirmed. Build a fixture where the publisher and the confirmer are the same identity and confirm the output makes that visible - surfacing the author-recruits-confirmers pattern while it is still free to attempt is section A.4's stated purpose, so a figure that hides it defeats the point of Phase A.

LIVE-LOG AND LIVE-REGISTRY HYGIENE: neither suite may write to .harness/logs/events.jsonl or .harness/precedents/. Measure and quote before/after. This is the twice-measured contamination defect (roughly 598 synthetic events at T-346; roughly 9,600 precedent-family events measured at T-352); a new contamination source is a REJECT.

SPEC CONFORMANCE, not just green tests: take T-368's numbered requirements for the enforcement and for the reputation surface and check EACH against the shipped code - one line per requirement id with PASS, FAIL or NOT-IMPLEMENTED. An unimplemented requirement that no test covers is exactly what a green suite hides, and finding it is the reason this task is control-plane tier.

RECORD-BEFORE-CODE (PR-017 procedure, AB5): confirm the authorizing records existed BEFORE the code - compare each record's published_at against T-369's completion and the code's file evidence - and that each CLI's behavior matches its record's ratio without exceeding it. Code that does MORE than its record authorizes is an unauthorized protocol change and a REJECT, even if it is a good idea.

VERDICT T-370 AND T-371 SEPARATELY, each via `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py update T-3NN --status done --agent <you> --note-file <f>` (or --status open with a REJECTED: note naming each defect). RECORD YOUR REVIEWER IDENTITY and confirm in writing that you produced no artifact in this epic, are not verifier-final or any verifier-v1-* identity, and are not the identity that executed T-373 or that will execute T-375. Role=verifier, so P-022 self-done applies provided your --agent differs from the creator; state that you used it.

Full adversarial replay of both artifacts already completed independently: four mandatory attacks run, both suites re-run (252 and 41, my own Ran N lines), spec conformance walked requirement by requirement across AD2-30..39 and AD2-50..69. T-370 and T-371 verdicted done separately with replayable evidence in each task JSON.

DECISION: T-374 EXECUTED AND COMPLETE. Control-plane-tier adversarial replay of both artifacts
run independently of both handoffs. VERDICTS: T-370 DONE, T-371 DONE, each recorded separately
with its own replayable evidence in .harness/tasks/T-370.json and .harness/tasks/T-371.json.
Neither artifact was rejected; two disclosed deviations in T-371 and one in T-370 were ruled on
explicitly and four open questions were forwarded to T-375 rather than absorbed.

  1  BOTH SUITES RE-RUN MYSELF, not trusted from the handoffs.
       test_precedent*.py   -> Ran 252 tests, OK   (> 229 required)
       test_reputation*.py  -> Ran 41 tests, OK    (>= 12 required)

  2  ATTACK 1 -- eleven refusal messages replayed under throwaway roots and compared
       character-for-character against section 3 and section 9.2; all exit 1. Each authorship
       element withheld in turn against BOTH target kinds. THIRTEEN bypass shapes attempted
       (empty string, whitespace, empty file, whitespace file, truncated, one-character-changed,
       case-folded, wrong record's ratio, record-id naming a different record, fabricated
       published_by, wrong issuing task, anchor marker smuggled onto a PR target, and

       correct-per-spec and I proved why: one was a byte-exact ratio that only looked truncated
       (PR-016's stored ratio has no trailing newline; cmp confirmed identity), the other is
       AD2-38's pre-declared boundary. Compliant calls verified on both target kinds with
       sha256 equality on the embedded ratio and section 9.2's expected output reproduced
       byte-for-byte.
  3  NEGATIVE CONTROL -- plain publish, cites/follows, supersedes and voids all exit 0 and all
       carry the new key present-but-null. The enforcement taxes no ordinary publish.
  4  ATTACK 2 -- 25 invocations covering every subcommand and every output path against the
       LIVE root, plus exit-4 paths against a fixture. 209 hashed stores and counters
       (31 records, blackboard.json, state.json, plan.md, 165 task records, events.jsonl line
       count and sha256, full .harness/ inventory). Aggregate sha256 identical before and
       after: e09221b8c52a30d090c89d387b0c4d5185df7217597cb19e7df9677d3e809c26. ZERO BYTES OF
       DRIFT. Full source grep reported with context: every write-primitive hit is inside the

  5  ATTACK 3 -- output paths enumerated from the code by me, then each run and grepped against
       LINE 789 OF THE SPEC DOCUMENT ITSELF rather than a retyped copy (141 bytes, exact match).
       18 of 18 figure-bearing and refusal paths carry it, as a named top-level first JSON key
       in --json. Two non-figure paths do not (exit 4, and the three argparse subparser --help
       pages); both ruled on and forwarded rather than silently passed or inflated to a reject.
  6  ATTACK 4 -- read from the code, not the docstring, on both files. reputation.py: PUBLIC_API
       exhaustive, clean signature audit against thirteen gate-shaped tokens, exactly two
       numeric comparisons in the whole file and both are display/count, no hardcoded identity
       special-casing, no monkeypatching, nothing importable as a gate. precedent.py: function-
       level diff against git HEAD shows qualifying_applications_count and cmd_confirm

       changed and nothing removed. No standing-keyed threshold anywhere.
  7  AB2 -- every figure carries its attribution string, literal-matched against AD2-56's table;
       the adjudications figure is present, null (never 0), and explicitly marked unavailable.

  9  HYGIENE -- events.jsonl 12808 before both suites, 12808 after. Aggregate md5 of every
       precedent record identical before and after; 31 records both times; file set diffed
       identical. Live conflicts: 1 finding (the pre-existing PR-001/P-023 dangling token),

 10  SPEC CONFORMANCE -- every numbered requirement walked one line at a time with PASS / FAIL /

FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS FORWARDED TO T-375, none of them blocking:
  OQ-A  exit 4 carries no caveat and no fixed --json shape, so AD2-61's text and the code agree
        in substance but disagree on paper. Needs a record, not a verifier's edit.
  OQ-B  the three subparser --help pages carry no caveat. One epilog= per subparser closes it.
  OQ-C  `identities --json` has no shape fixed anywhere in section 5 and T-372 is about to quote
        the surface into a tracked constitutional document. Freeze the shape by record BEFORE
        T-372 quotes it, or T-372 makes an undisclosed planner judgment load-bearing. This is
        the one worth acting on first.
  OQ-D  the live registry carries THREE records with subject westphalia-kpi (PR-029, PR-030,
        PR-031), all worker-a2-3 / T-369, all active. I confirmed the duplication by grouping
        every record by subject. Mtimes place all three before either artifact, so it is T-369's
        residue and T-373 has already verdicted T-369 done. Worth naming: `conflicts` does NOT
        flag it, because detector 1 excludes already-related pairs and non-contradictory
        same-subject ratios -- a duplicate publish of one ledger row is invisible to the sweep.
        PR-031 also lists two of its citation tokens twice.
  Also recorded: AD2-43 instructs a hash check that cannot pass as written (six of PR-001..
  PR-017 have appended cited_by entries). The mechanism is authorized and benign, but the
  instruction should be restated as "no immutable field changed" before a future verifier reads
  a true hash mismatch as tampering.

I wrote no source file and acquired no write lock, because this task produces no artifact: its
deliverable is the two verdicts and the evidence behind them, both now recorded on the board.
